text: The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
Get up and go to the great city of Nineveh, and speak out against it, because word of its wickedness has reached me.

But Jonah got up to run away from the LORD's presence, heading for Tarshish instead. He went down to Joppa, found a ship sailing that way, paid his fare, and boarded it to go with them to Tarshish, away from the LORD.
But the LORD threw a great wind out over the sea, and so violent a storm arose that the ship threatened to come apart.

The sailors were terrified, and each one called out to his own god. They began throwing the ship's cargo into the sea to lighten it. Meanwhile Jonah had gone down into the hold, lain down, and fallen into a deep sleep.
The captain came to him and said, How can you be asleep? Get up and call on your god — perhaps he will take notice of us, and we won't be lost.
Then the crew said to each other, Come, let's cast lots to find out who is to blame for this trouble. So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
So they said to him, Tell us — who has brought this disaster on us? What is your business, where are you from, what is your country, and what people are you from?
He answered, I am a Hebrew, and I worship the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made both the sea and the dry ground.
At this the men were seized with great fear, and they asked him, What have you done? — because they now knew he was running from the LORD's presence, since he had told them so.
The sea was growing rougher, so they asked him, What should we do with you to make it calm again?
He told them, Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and it will grow calm — I know this great storm has come on you because of me.
Instead, the men rowed hard to get back to land, but they couldn't, because the sea kept growing wilder against them.
So they cried out to the LORD, Please, LORD, don't let us die for this man's life, and don't hold us guilty of innocent blood — for you, LORD, have done just as you pleased.
Then they picked Jonah up and threw him into the sea, and its raging stopped at once.
The men were filled with great fear of the LORD, and they offered a sacrifice to him and made vows.
And the LORD provided a huge fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah remained inside the fish for three days and three nights.
